{
  "need": "Status",
  "secondary": { "name": "Belonging" },
  "read": "This player is hungry to be seen and recognized, probably because good performances feel invisible in a team sport where the group gets the credit. The showboating is a homemade status system — if no one else is conferring respect loudly enough, they'll take it themselves. The irony is the behavior is costing them the teammates' regard they actually want.",
  "pull": { "collapse": "Enforcer", "instinct": "Call them out in front of the group or run them for it — feels like accountability but it publicly humiliates them, which attacks the exact status need driving the behavior and turns the locker room into a courtroom with you as judge." },
  "mentorMove": "Pull them aside one-on-one, name the good play genuinely first, then be straight that the celebration is landing wrong with the team and costing their own reputation — frame it as protecting their status, not erasing it.",
  "holdFirm": [
    "The standard is that we celebrate together or we move to the next play — individual showboating is off the table.",
    "Teammates' experience of the culture is non-negotiable; one person's highlight reel does not outweigh the room."
  ],
  "stayFlexible": [
    "Let them keep some personality and energy in how they celebrate — a fist pump, a word to a teammate — as long as it pulls people in rather than putting people down.",
    "Find a real public moment to recognize their contribution loudly in front of the group so they don't feel they have to manufacture it themselves."
  ],
  "forceLevel": { "level": 1, "label": "Empathy" },
  "script": [
    { "phase": "Connection", "words": "Hey, come here a second. That play was legit — your footwork on that was sharp and I want you to know I saw it." },
    { "phase": "Curiosity", "words": "Let me ask you something honest: when you do the big celebration after a play like that, what are you going for? Because I want to understand what you're looking for." },
    { "phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Here's what I'm seeing from where I stand. The guys are going quiet when it happens, and that quiet is actually shrinking your reputation with them, not building it. You're too good for your highlight to get overshadowed by that. So let's figure out how you carry yourself after a big play in a way that makes this whole group look at you like a leader instead of tuning you out." },
    { "phase": "Commitment", "words": "I'm holding you to this because my standard for you is higher than the average player and I genuinely believe you can lead this group — not just perform in it. Next big play, I want to see you point to whoever set you up or just get back on defense like you knew it was coming. Can you do that for me this week?" }
  ],
  "longGame": "Keep recognizing this player's specific contributions publicly and consistently so they stop feeling starved for acknowledgment — a player who feels genuinely seen by their coach doesn't need to perform for the crowd, and over time they'll start channeling that hunger into pulling teammates up instead of stepping over them."
}
situation: A player showboats after good plays and it is rubbing teammates the wrong way.
